PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED — ITS "WHAT IS OWED" CLAUSE IS DELIVERED, AND NOTHING ELSE IN IT MOVED. It closes: *"a served surface that answers 'what version am I talking to?' WITHOUT depending on a file the installer may not have written. `loop_status.served_by.reflow2_version` already computes it; nothing puts it where a friction report would pick it up."*

`<graph>.client.json` is now written at every `initialize`, carrying `reflow2_version` alongside the client's name, its version, and the negotiated MCP revision. It does not depend on the installer having written anything. And `report-friction` was changed in the same PR to read the environment block out of it — so it is now precisely where a friction report picks it up.

🛑 THE MEASUREMENT ITSELF IS UNTOUCHED AND STAYS OPEN. Its subject is a past event — dev_storyflow filing a defect eighteen hours after it was fixed, while running a pre-#303 binary and reporting *"kit-version.json absent — could not read a version."* That happened; a dated observation of a past event does not become false. Its central claim also still stands in full: an agent that cannot name its version cannot tell a live defect from a closed one, and 2026-08-27 supplied a second instance — a reporter talking to 0.39.0 while the kit stamp said 0.11.0.

⚠️ AND ITS SECOND HALF IS UNADDRESSED: *"the same trap is live on this side"* — `served_by.stale` reporting a replaced executable. Nothing here touched that.

📌 FOUND BY SEARCH, NOT BY THE COMPUTATION. `unclaimed_findings` on this session's ChangeEvents returned 17 candidates and this was not among them, because its `subject_id` is `req:declared-vocabulary-is-reachable-from-the-surface` and no change event touched that node. That is the documented limit — the computation reaches what is anchored — and the capture-session skill's instruction to search when you still suspect something is what found it.
